3. The Prompt As Conditioning Text

This connects back to next token prediction being conditioned on everything seen so far, already covered in Next Token Prediction. A prompt is genuinely nothing more than the text a model conditions its very first prediction on.
Everything genuinely generated afterward flows directly from that genuinely initial conditioning text, a genuinely simple but powerful framing explored throughout the rest of this topic.
4. Zero Shot Prompting
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292297-564075327.png
This connects back to the prompt as conditioning text, already covered in this topic. The genuinely simplest style asks a task directly, with genuinely no examples given at all.
The model genuinely relies entirely on knowledge already learned during training to respond, a genuinely minimal prompting style explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 5. Few Shot Prompting
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292297-155178511.png
This connects back to zero-shot prompting, already covered in this topic. A genuinely richer style includes a genuinely small handful of example input-output pairs directly inside the prompt.
The model genuinely infers the intended pattern from those examples before answering the actual real question, a genuinely effective technique explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This pattern-inference behavior, already covered in this topic, directly explains why few-shot prompting often works well for tasks with a genuinely specific output format that zero-shot prompting alone struggles to reliably produce.

blocks.text: 6. Prompt Structure And Roles
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292297-709645034.png
This connects back to few-shot prompting, already covered in this topic. Genuinely real chat-style prompts typically separate text into distinct roles, like system, user, and assistant.
Each genuinely role gives the model a different kind of guidance about how to treat that particular piece of text, a genuinely structural convention explored throughout the rest of this topic.
7. Prompt Sensitivity
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292298-212439137.png
This connects back to prompt structure and roles, already covered in this topic. Genuinely small wording changes in a prompt can genuinely produce noticeably different model output.
This genuinely sensitivity is exactly why prompt wording is treated as a genuinely real, iterative design task, a genuinely practical reality explored throughout the rest of this topic.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates building a zero-shot and a few-shot prompt, already covered in this topic, for the same simple task.

code.content:
def zero_shot_prompt(task):
    # already covered as zero-shot prompting in this topic
    return f"Task: {task}\nAnswer:"

def few_shot_prompt(task, examples):
    # already covered as few-shot prompting in this topic
    example_text = "\n".join(f"Input: {inp}\nOutput: {out}" for inp, out in examples)
    return f"{example_text}\nInput: {task}\nOutput:"

task = "translate 'good morning' to French"

zero_shot = zero_shot_prompt(task)
print("Zero-shot prompt (already covered in this topic):")
print(zero_shot)

examples = [("hello", "bonjour"), ("thank you", "merci")]
few_shot = few_shot_prompt(task, examples)
print("\nFew-shot prompt (already covered in this topic):")
print(few_shot)

# already covered as prompts consuming context window budget in this topic
print(f"\nZero-shot token estimate: {len(zero_shot.split())} words")
print(f"Few-shot token estimate: {len(few_shot.split())} words")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the few-shot prompt using noticeably more tokens than the zero-shot prompt, exactly the context window budget tradeoff already covered in this topic, in exchange for showing the model a clearer pattern.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Prompting is the craft of writing input text that steers a model toward a useful output.
A prompt is simply the text a model conditions its very first prediction on.
Zero-shot prompting asks a task directly, relying entirely on the model's own trained knowledge.
Few-shot prompting includes a handful of examples, letting the model infer the intended pattern.
Real chat-style prompts often separate text into roles, like system, user, and assistant.
Small wording changes in a prompt can produce noticeably different output, a real sensitivity.
Every token spent on prompt instructions and examples eats into the fixed context window budget.
Zero-shot suits simple, well known tasks; few-shot suits tasks needing a less standard format.
